object_type: Wall painting fragment, Tomb-chapel of Nebamun: Inspecting Cattle and Herdsmen
findspot: Tomb-chapel of Nebamun, Dra Abu el-Naga, Thebes, Upper Egypt
description: Fragment of a polychrome tomb painting from the Tomb-chapel of Nebamun at Thebes. Nebamun, scribe and grain accountant at the Temple of Amun, inspects herds of cattle brought before him. Herdsmen lead and present long-horned and hornless oxen, while an elderly, balding herdsman kneels before Nebamun offering obeisance. Scribes with papyrus rolls and reed pens stand by to record the official livestock count. The hieroglyphic captions record the dialogue of the herdsmen praising Nebamun.

object_type: Wall painting fragment, Tomb-chapel of Nebamun: Counting Geese and Poultry
findspot: Tomb-chapel of Nebamun, Dra Abu el-Naga, Thebes, Upper Egypt
description: Fragment of a painted limestone wall panel from the Tomb-chapel of Nebamun depicting the counting of domesticated geese and waterfowl. Agricultural laborers and poultry keepers present flocks of white and grey geese; one herdsman holds open a wicker basket coop while other birds are lined up in registers. Scribes bow and present inscribed papyrus scrolls recording the exact tally for the estate accounts.

object_type: Wall painting fragment, Tomb-chapel of Nebamun: Assessing the Crops of the Estates
findspot: Tomb-chapel of Nebamun, Dra Abu el-Naga, Thebes, Upper Egypt
description: Polychrome wall painting from the Tomb-chapel of Nebamun illustrating estate agricultural administration. Estate workers and farmers gather to report on crop yields. Scribes hold writing tablets and recording palettes, verifying measurements and recording the harvest figures for the grain stores of the Amun temple complex.

file: File:Tomb of Nebamun, horse and chariot.jpg
object_type: Wall painting fragment, Tomb-chapel of Nebamun: Surveying the Fields and Harvesting Grain
findspot: Tomb-chapel of Nebamun, Dra Abu el-Naga, Thebes, Upper Egypt
description: Painted wall fragment from the Tomb-chapel of Nebamun showing agricultural field work and cadastral surveying. In the lower register, field laborers reap tall ripe emmer wheat using curved sickles. In the upper register, surveyors stretch a knotted measuring rope across the fields to assess agricultural boundaries and tax liabilities. A chariot with two spirited horses and an attendant rests beneath the shade of a sycamore fig tree.

file: File:Escriba en la tumba de Nebamun (British Museum).jpg
object_type: Wall painting detail, Tomb-chapel of Nebamun: The Scribe of Accounts
findspot: Tomb-chapel of Nebamun, Dra Abu el-Naga, Thebes, Upper Egypt
description: Close detail of an ancient Egyptian scribe from the Tomb-chapel of Nebamun. The scribe is depicted seated cross-legged on a mat with a long unrolled papyrus document across his lap, dipping a reed brush into an ink palette containing cakes of black and red ink. Scribes formed the administrative backbone of ancient Egyptian labor, recording rations, work quotas, estate yields, and artisan assignments.

file: File:Egyptian Wood Model of Boat, 12th Dynasty (36617631765).jpg
object_type: Model, river boat with rowers and sailors
findspot: Beni Hasan, Middle Egypt
description: Painted wooden tomb model of a Nile transport boat manned by a crew of rowers, deckhands, and a steersman operating a large steering oar. Transport along the Nile was essential for ancient Egyptian trade, grain distribution, stone transport for monuments, and troop movements. Such models were placed in Middle Kingdom tombs to ensure transportation in the afterlife.

object_type: Attic black-figure neck-amphora: The Olive Harvest
findspot: Vulci, Etruria (produced in Athens, Greece)
description: Attic black-figure amphora attributed to the Antimenes Painter depicting the olive harvest, one of the most famous Greek representations of agricultural labor. In an olive grove, two men have climbed into the branches of an olive tree and beat the boughs with long poles to knock ripe olives loose. A bearded man at the base strikes the trunk, while a naked youth scrambles on his knees on the ground collecting olives into a deep woven wicker basket.

file: File:Eye-kylix type A - ABV extra - potter assembling a kylix - Athena fighting giant - London BM - 1847-1125-18 - 01.jpg
object_type: Attic black-figure eye-kylix: Potter at Work on the Wheel
findspot: Attica, Greece
description: Attic black-figure eye-kylix (Type A, Cat. Vases B 432). The interior tondo depicts an ancient Greek potter seated beside a low turntable wheel, carefully assembling a kylix and attaching a clay handle. Behind him on a workshop wall shelf are arranged four finished kylikes and an oinochoe jug drying before firing. Exterior features large protective eyes and Athena fighting a giant in gigantomachy.

file: File:Pasiades Painter ARV 98 1 two running women and a heron (01).jpg
object_type: Attic white-ground alabastron: Signed by Master Potter Pasiades
findspot: Marion-Arsinoe (Tomb 162), Cyprus (produced in Athens, Greece)
description: Attic white-ground perfume flask (alabastron, Cat. Vases B 668) featuring the signature of the master potter Pasiades: 'PASIADES EPOIESEN' ('Pasiades made it') stamped onto the mouth. Decorated by the Pasiades Painter with a heron standing between two running maenads. Signed ceramic vessels illustrate the pride and social standing of Athenian ceramic workshop proprietors and master craftsmen.

object_type: Bronze statuette: Archaic Greek Ploughman with Team of Oxen
findspot: Boeotia, Greece (or Asia Minor)
description: Archaic Greek solid-cast bronze group (Cat. Bronze 180) representing an agricultural laborer guiding a two-ox team. The farmer wears a simple tunic and leans forward over a primitive ard-plow, steadying the wooden handle with both hands while driving the yoked pair of horned draft oxen through furrowed earth. Demonstrates primary tillage technology used across ancient Mediterranean farms.

object_type: Marble funerary stele: The Shoemaker Xanthippos
findspot: Athens, Greece
description: Classical Athenian marble grave relief (Cat. Sculpture 628) of Xanthippos. The deceased artisan is shown as a mature bearded man seated in profile on an elegant klismos chair, with his two small daughters standing before him. In his right hand, Xanthippos proudly holds up a shoemaker's last (kalopous), the primary carved wooden form used by cobblers and shoemakers to shape leather footwear, proudly commemorating his skilled profession.

file: File:Marble relief with portraits of the freedmen Publius Licinius Philonicus and Publius Licinius Demetrius, British Museum.jpg
object_type: Marble funerary relief: Freedmen Artisans Publius Licinius Philonicus & Demetrius
findspot: Near Frascati (ancient Tusculum), Lazio, Italy
description: Marble funerary monument celebrating two Roman freedmen (liberti): Publius Licinius Philonicus and Publius Licinius Demetrius. In the central niches are realistic portrait busts of the two former slaves in Roman togas. Flanking the pediments and fascia are carved instruments of their specialized trades: at left, the blacksmith and coin minter's anvil, tongs, and coining die hammer; at right, the carpenter and joiner's adze, double axe, and folding measuring rule.

object_type: Marble relief: Roman Sailor Navigating a Cargo Vessel (Corbita)
findspot: Carthage, Roman Africa Proconsularis (modern Tunisia)
description: Roman marble architectural relief (Cat. Sculpture 2405) showing an ancient sailor maneuvering a corbita, a round-hulled Mediterranean merchant vessel used to transport olive oil amphorae, wine, and grain from North Africa to Rome. The helmsman stands at the stern gripping the steering oar (gubernaculum), managing the vessel under full sail across the waves.

object_type: Surgical instruments: Roman Bronze Catheters and Probes
findspot: Italy
description: Set of finely wrought Roman bronze surgical instruments (GR 1968.6-26.1–39), including S-shaped male catheters, curved specula, and probes. Professional Roman physicians (medici) and military camp surgeons used specialized medical kits for operations, suturing wounds, and treating bladder obstructions. Demonstrates high technical precision in Roman metalwork and medical professions.

object_type: Vindolanda Ink Writing Tablet: Commercial Grain, Hides, and Sinews Account (Tablet 343)
material: Alder and birch wood, carbon ink
findspot: Vindolanda Roman Fort (Chesterholm), Northumberland, Roman Britain
description: Wafer-thin wooden leaf tablet written in Latin cursive using carbon ink, discovered in anaerobic waterlogged soil at the Roman fort of Vindolanda near Hadrian's Wall. Tablet 343 is a business letter from Octavius to Candidus discussing commercial deliveries: purchasing 100 modii of wheat, transporting cow hides, collecting sinew for military equipment, and financial settlements with regional traders and tanners.

file: File:Early writing tablet recording the allocation of beer.jpg
object_type: Proto-Cuneiform Clay Tablet: Daily Beer and Grain Rations for Laborers (BM 140855)
findspot: Southern Mesopotamia (modern southern Iraq)
description: One of the earliest administrative accounting documents in human history. Written in proto-cuneiform pictograms, this clay tablet records rations of barley beer and bread allotted to groups of state and temple laborers. The pictographic signs include a human head next to a triangular bowl (representing 'eating/rationing') and a pointed conical jar (representing 'beer'). Laborers in Mesopotamia were compensated with daily grain and beer rations.

file: File:Winged bull leaving the quarry WA 124820.jpg
object_type: Neo-Assyrian Gypsum Relief: Transport of Winged Bull: Hauling out of Quarry (WA 124820)
findspot: Southwest Palace of Sennacherib, Court VI, Nineveh, Northern Iraq
description: Monumental palace wall relief from Nineveh illustrating the monumental logistics of royal construction. A colossal human-headed winged bull (lamassu) weighing over 30 tons is loaded onto a massive wooden sledge in the limestone quarry at Balatai. Quarrymen and construction workers use long timber levers, wedges, and thick ropes to maneuver the sledge out of the pit, while overseers coordinate the work.

object_type: Neo-Assyrian Gypsum Relief: Transport of Winged Bull: Tool-Bearers and Road Crews (WA 124821)
findspot: Southwest Palace of Sennacherib, Court VI, Nineveh, Northern Iraq
description: Panel from the Sennacherib bull-transport frieze depicting support labor work gangs preparing the path for the colossal sledge. Laborers march in organized columns carrying crosscut saws, hatchets, pickaxes, and wicker baskets piled high with gravel and earth to level hills, build ramps, and clear obstacles along the transport corridor.

file: File:Workmen pulling the winged bull WA 124822.jpg
object_type: Neo-Assyrian Gypsum Relief: Transport of Winged Bull: Work Gangs Pulling on Sledge (WA 124822)
findspot: Southwest Palace of Sennacherib, Court VI, Nineveh, Northern Iraq
description: Relief panel depicting hundreds of conscripted laborers and prisoners of war pulling four thick cables attached to the front of the wooden sledge carrying the colossal bull. Taskmasters armed with clubs and sticks walk alongside the lines urging the teams forward, while directors with hand trumpets signal coordinated pulling surges.

object_type: Neo-Assyrian Gypsum Relief: Transport of Winged Bull: Rollers and Shaduf Water-Lifters (WA 124823)
findspot: Southwest Palace of Sennacherib, Court VI, Nineveh, Northern Iraq
description: Relief panel showing mechanical techniques used by Assyrian engineers to move massive stones over marshy ground. Workers lift heavy wooden rollers that have emerged behind the sledge and run them forward to place beneath the advancing runners. In the background along the riverbank, agricultural workers operate shadufs (counterweighted lever water-lifters) to irrigate fields or wet transport tracks.

file: File:Royal inscription winged bull reliefs WA 124824.jpg
object_type: Neo-Assyrian Gypsum Relief: Transport of Winged Bull: Palace Ramp and Inscription (WA 124824)
findspot: Southwest Palace of Sennacherib, Court VI, Nineveh, Northern Iraq
description: Final panel of the Nineveh bull-transport sequence showing the colossal bull arriving at the palace gates up an earthen ramp. King Sennacherib stands in his royal chariot observing the work, while master architects, scribes, and engineers supervise the placement of the monument. Inscribed above is a cuneiform text recording Sennacherib's building achievements and the mobilization of imperial labor.
